questions.solution:
Given that the wickets taken by five bowlers A, B, C, D and E are all different.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. Wickets taken by C are less than both E and B, but more than A.

→ **E, B > C > A**

2. Wickets taken by D are the least.

→ **E, B > C > A > D**

3. B has taken **12 wickets**.

→ Since C has taken fewer wickets than B, **C → **E > B(12) > C > A(8) > D**

Thus, the possible number of wickets taken by **A** is **8**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question: Weight of 6 boys P, Q, R, S, T and V is compared. Weight of no two boys is same. Number of boys having weight more than P are same as number of boys having weight less than T. Weight of R is more than only V and T. Weight P is less than only S. Weight of how many boys is more than T?
questions.solution:
Given that there are **6 boys** P, Q, R, S, T and V with different weights.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. R is heavier than only V and T.

→ This means the order from heaviest to lightest is:

→ _ > _ > _ > R > T > V

2. P is lighter than only S.

→ So, S is the heaviest and P is the second heaviest.

→ S > P > _ > R > T > V

3. Number of boys heavier than P equals the number of boys lighter than T.

→ Boys heavier than P = 1 (only S).

→ Therefore, boys lighter than T must also be 1 (only V), which matches the arrangement.

Thus, the final order from heaviest to lightest is:

→ **S > P > Q > R > T > V**

Boys heavier than T are: **S, P, Q and R**.

Hence, the number of boys heavier than T is **4**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question: What is the angle (in degrees) between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 1:10 PM?
questions.solution:
The given time is **1:10 PM**.

Angle covered by the **hour hand** from the 12 o'clock position:

For 1 hour and 10 minutes = (1 × 30°) + (10 × 1/2°)

= 30° + 5° = 35°

Angle covered by the **minute hand** from the 12 o'clock position:

For 10 minutes = 10 × 6° = 60°

The **angle between the hour and minute hands** = |60° − 35°| = 25°

Hence, the angle between the hands is **25°**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the hour hand and minute hand = |60H - 11M| over 2

Here, **H = 1** and **M = 10**.

Angle = |(60 times 1 - 11 times 10)| over 2

Angle = |60 − 110| / 2

Angle = |−50| / 2 = 50/2 = 25°

Therefore, the correct answer is **25**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** Hour hand covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 30°

Angular distance covered in 60 minutes = 30°

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 30/60 = 1/2°

Minute hand covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360/60 = 6°

questions.question: A watch is 6 minutes slow at 3 PM. It gains 12 seconds every hour. When will it show the correct time (in PM) again?
questions.solution:
The watch is **6 minutes slow** at **3 PM**.

Rate of gain = **12 seconds per hour**.

First, we convert the initial lag from minutes into seconds:

Initial lag = 6 × 60 = **360 seconds**

Now, calculate the number of hours the watch needs to run to gain back these 360 seconds:

Number of hours = 360 ÷ 12 = **30 hours**

To find the time when the watch will show the correct time, add **30 hours** to the starting time of **3 PM**:

30 hours = 24 hours + 6 hours

Adding 24 hours to 3 PM gives **3 PM the next day**.

Adding the remaining 6 hours to 3 PM: 3 PM + 6 hours = **9 PM**.

Hence, the watch will show the **correct time** at **9:00 PM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 3**”.

questions.question: Who presides over the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the vice-president?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 89** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Vice-President of India** is the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• In the **absence** of the **Chairman**, the **Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** presides over the sittings of the House as per **Article 91**.
 
• The **Deputy Chairman** is elected by the members of the **Rajya Sabha** from among themselves; unlike the **Chairman**, they must be a member of the House.
 
• While acting as the **presiding officer**, the **Deputy Chairman** possesses all the powers and duties of the **Chairman**, including the power to maintain **decorum** and the right to exercise a **casting vote** in case of a tie.
 
• It is important to note that the **Deputy Chairman** is not subordinate to the **Chairman**; they are directly responsible to the **Rajya Sabha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of Lok Sabha**:

 
 
• The **Speaker** is the **presiding officer** of the **Lower House** (Lok Sabha).
 
• In a **joint sitting** of both Houses of **Parliament**, the **Speaker** presides, and in their absence, the **Deputy Speaker** or the **Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** takes the chair.
 
 
 
• **President**:
 
 
• The **President** is the **Executive Head** of the **Union** but does not preside over either House.
 
• If the offices of both **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman** are **vacant**, the **President** appoints a member of the **Rajya Sabha** to perform the duties of the **Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the **Head of the Council of Ministers** and the leader of the House (if they are a member of that House).
 
• They do not hold a **constitutional role** in presiding over the parliamentary sessions.
 
 
 
• **Panel of Vice-Chairpersons**:
 
 
• The **Chairman** nominates a panel of **Vice-Chairpersons** who can preside over the **Rajya Sabha** when both the **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman** are **absent**.

questions.question: What are Boliyan in the context of Giddha dance?

options.text: Types of costumes worn by dancers
Traditional songs sung during the dance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Traditional songs sung during the dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boliyan** (singular: Boli) are the rhythmic folk couplets or verses that form the lyrical foundation of the **Giddha** dance, a premier folk art performed by women in the **Punjab** region.
 
• These songs are traditionally transmitted through oral tradition and are central to the performance, as the dancers move and clap in synchronization with the rhythm and meaning of the lyrics.
 
• During a performance, a lead woman typically recites the **Boli**, and as the narrative reaches its peak or **Tappa**, the other dancers join in with high-pitched vocals and vigorous movements.
 
• The themes of **Boliyan** are diverse, covering various facets of Punjabi life including **social issues**, **agricultural cycles**, **family dynamics**, and emotional expressions of love, joy, or satire.
 
• Historically, these songs served as a medium for women to voice their perspectives on domestic life, often using humor to critique the **Saas-Bahu** (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) relationship or to celebrate weddings and festivals like **Teeyan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giddha Dance Characteristics**:

 
 
• It is considered the feminine counterpart to **Bhangra** and is known for its grace, speed, and spontaneous energy.
 
• The dance is usually performed in a circle, and unlike many other folk dances, it does not strictly require musical instruments, as rhythmic **clapping** (Thapi) provides the primary beat.
 
• Costumes for **Giddha** include vibrant **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** paired with **Phulkari** (traditional embroidery) dupattas and heavy jewelry like **Suggi-Phul**.
 
 
 
• **Musical Elements**:
 
 
• While the human voice is the main component, sometimes a **Dhol** (drum) or a **Ghara** (earthen pot) is used to enhance the rhythm.
 
• The **Boliyan** are distinct from the dance steps themselves, which involve mimicking daily activities like churning milk or spinning a **Charkha**.

questions.question: Which Indian lake is of volcanic origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lonar Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lonar Lake** is situated in the **Buldhana district** of **Maharashtra** and is uniquely characterized as a **crater lake** formed within the **Deccan Traps**, which is a large **volcanic igneous province**.
 
• While modern geological studies confirm it was created by a **meteorite impact** approximately 52,000 years ago during the **Pleistocene Epoch**, it is categorized as a lake of volcanic origin in many contexts because it is the only known impact crater in the world formed in **basaltic rock**.
 
• The lake is **endorheic**, meaning it has no outflow, leading to high levels of **salinity** and **alkalinity** (pH levels reaching up to 10.5).
 
• It was designated as a **Ramsar site** in **November 2020**, identifying it as a wetland of international importance.
 
• The lake gained global attention in 2020 when its water turned **pink** due to the presence of **Haloarchaea**, a salt-loving microbial population.
 
• It is protected as a **National Geo-heritage Monument** by the **Geological Survey of India** (GSI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sambhar Lake**:

 
 
• Located in **Rajasthan**, it is the largest **inland salt lake** in India.
 
• It is a **Ramsar site** and a major source of India's salt production.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake**:
 
 
• Located in **Manipur**, it is the largest **freshwater lake** in Northeast India.
 
• It is famous for **Phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation) and the **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, the world's only floating national park.
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake**:
 
 
• Situated in **Odisha**, it is the largest **brackish water lagoon** in India.
 
• It was the first Indian wetland to be designated under the **Ramsar Convention** in 1981 and hosts **Irrawaddy dolphins**.

questions.question: Who was the only person to be elected president of India as an independent candidate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V. V. Giri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Varahagiri Venkata Giri**, popularly known as **V. V. Giri**, served as the **fourth President of India** from **24 August 1969** to **24 August 1974**.
 
• He holds the unique distinction of being the only person in the history of the **Republic of India** to be elected as an **Independent candidate** for the post of President.
 
• The **1969 Presidential Election** was a turning point in Indian politics; although the official **Indian National Congress** candidate was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, the then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** supported Giri.
 
• Giri won the election after a famous call for a **conscience vote** by **Indira Gandhi**, which led to a narrow victory over the party's official nominee and eventually caused a split in the **Congress Party**.
 
• Prior to his full term, he served as the **Vice-President of India** and became the **Acting President** following the sudden demise of **Dr. Zakir Husain** in **May 1969**.
 
• He was a prominent **trade union leader** and served as the **Union Minister of Labour**, besides holding various gubernatorial positions in states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Kerala**, and **Mysore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**:

 
 
• He served as the **sixth President of India** (1977–1982) and is the only person to be elected **unopposed** to the office.
 
• He also served as the **Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh** and the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Zail Singh**:
 
 
• He was the **seventh President of India** (1982–1987) and the first **Sikh** to hold the highest constitutional office.
 
• He is noted for using his **pocket veto** power against the **Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill** in 1986.
 
 
 
• **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed**:
 
 
• He was the **fifth President of India** (1974–1977) and the second President to **die in office**.
 
• His presidency is notably associated with the signing of the **Proclamation of Emergency** in **June 1975**.

questions.question: What is the standard court size for women in Kabaddi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12m × 8m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard dimensions for a **Kabaddi** court intended for **Women** and **Junior Boys** are **12 meters** in length and **8 meters** in width, as mandated by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)**.
 
• The court is divided into two equal halves by a **midline**, resulting in two playing areas each measuring **6 meters × 8 meters**.
 
• The **Baulk Line** in the women’s court is marked at a distance of **3 meters** from the midline on both sides.
 
• The **Bonus Line** is situated **1 meter** beyond the baulk line towards the end line (parallel to the midline).
 
• The **Lobby** refers to the **1-meter** wide strips on both sides of the court; these areas are active only after a struggle has commenced between the raider and the defenders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variations in Court Size**:

 
 
• For **Men** and **Senior Boys**, the standard court size is larger, measuring **13 meters × 10 meters**.
 
• For **Sub-Junior Boys and Girls**, the court size is reduced to **11 meters × 8 meters** to accommodate younger athletes.
 
 
 
• **Match Duration**:
 
 
• In the women’s category, a standard match consists of two halves of **15 minutes** each, with a **5-minute interval**.
 
• Men’s matches are longer, featuring two halves of **20 minutes** each.

questions.question: Average of 8 consecutive odd natural numbers is 40. The just previous and the just next odd natural number to these 8 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the new average?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of **consecutive numbers** in an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the **average** is the **middle term** or the **midpoint** of the series.

If we add **equal number of terms** on both the **left** (previous) and **right** (next) sides of an existing symmetric series, the **central point** (average) remains **unchanged**.

In this case, 1 odd number is added to the left and 1 odd number is added to the right, maintaining the **symmetry** around the original average of 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 8 **consecutive odd natural numbers** is 40.

**Formula Used:** Average of an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a8ca702cd9421024983420a776a18c8d6321532b3c863252fa7a9917c0aad05.png] 

⇒ For 8 consecutive odd numbers, the **average (40)** lies exactly between the 4th and 5th terms.

⇒ 4th term = 40 − 1 = 39; 5th term = 40 + 1 = 41.

⇒ The 8 numbers are: 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47.

⇒ **Just previous** odd number = 33 − 2 = 31.

⇒ **Just next** odd number = 47 + 2 = 49.

⇒ New set of 10 numbers: 31, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49.

⇒ New Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 = (31 + 49) ÷ 2

⇒ New Average = 80 ÷ 2 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

For any series with a common difference **d**, Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

If **k** terms are added to the beginning and **k** terms are added to the end of a consecutive series, the **mean** remains constant if the terms added are equidistant from the original center.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of first **n** odd natural numbers is always **n²**, and their average is **n**.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The chef is preparing a gourmet meal for the gala tonight.

options.text: A gourmet meal was being prepared by the chef for the gala tonight.
A gourmet meal is being prepared by the chef for the gala tonight.
A gourmet meal has been prepared by the chef for the gala tonight.
A gourmet meal is prepared by the chef for the gala tonight.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A gourmet meal is being prepared by the chef for the gala tonight.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Present Continuous Tense**, indicated by the auxiliary verb **is** followed by the **present participle** form of the verb **preparing**.

• The standard rule for converting **Present Continuous Tense** from active to **Passive Voice** follows the structure: **New Subject + is/am/are + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object**.

• The **Object** of the active sentence, **a gourmet meal**, transitions to the **Subject** position in the passive sentence.

• Because **a gourmet meal** is a **singular noun**, the auxiliary verb **is** is used, followed by the marker **being** to preserve the **continuous** nature of the action.

• The **Past Participle** of the verb **prepare** is **prepared**, which is used to satisfy the passive construction requirements.

• The **Subject** of the active sentence, **The chef**, becomes the **Agent** in the passive sentence and is introduced by the preposition **by**.

• The adverbial phrase **for the gala tonight** remains intact as it describes the **temporal and situational context** of the action.

 **Additional Information__**

• The distinction between different tenses in **Passive Voice** is crucial for selection:

• **Simple Present Passive**: Uses **is/am/are + V3** (e.g., is prepared). It is typically used for **facts or habits**.

• **Past Continuous Passive**: Uses **was/were + being + V3** (e.g., was being prepared). It describes an **interrupted or ongoing action** in the past.

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Uses **has/have + been + V3** (e.g., has been prepared). It indicates an **action completed** at an indefinite time in the past with current relevance.

</ul

• When converting this to **Passive Voice**, the structure changes to: **Is/Am/Are + New Subject (the original object) + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object (the original subject)?**.

• The object of the active sentence is **a book signing event**. As this is a **singular noun**, the auxiliary verb **Is** remains appropriate for the start of the passive sentence.

• The verb **organising** must be converted into the passive continuous form, which is **being organised**.

• Following these grammatical rules, the construction becomes: **Is** (Auxiliary) + **a book signing event** (New Subject) + **being organised** (Passive Verb) + **by the publishers** (Agent) + **for the new author** (Recipient phrase).

 **Additional Information__**

• **Tense Consistency:** Passive voice must always maintain the **original tense**. Using **Was** shifts the sentence into the **Past Continuous**, which is grammatically incorrect for this context.

• **Being vs. Been:** The word **being** is used for **continuous tenses**, while **been** is used for **perfect tenses** (e.g., Has a book signing event **been** organised?).

• **Logical Meaning:** The passive voice should not alter the **logical relationship** between the actors; the publishers are the ones performing the action, not the author.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Let this mistake not be repeated.

options.text: No one will repeat this mistake.
This mistake let not be repeated

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Don't repeat this mistake.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provided sentence 'Let this mistake not be repeated' is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the structure of a **Negative Imperative Sentence**.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, the construction for imperative sentences typically begins with **Let**, followed by the **Object**, then 'not' (for negative), the auxiliary **be**, and the **Past Participle (V3)** form of the verb.
 
• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the sentence must start with the **Imperative Verb** or the negative marker **Do not (Don't)** because the subject 'You' is understood and omitted in such commands.
 
• The conversion follows the formula: **Do not / Don't + Verb (Base Form) + Object**.
 
• Identifying the components: The object is **'this mistake'** and the principal verb is **'repeat'**. Combining these according to the active voice rule results in **'Don't repeat this mistake'**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voice Transformation Rules**:
 
 
• **Imperative Sentences**: These express orders, requests, or advice. In the **Active Voice**, they usually begin with a verb. Example: 'Shut the door' (Active) becomes 'Let the door be shut' (Passive).
 
• **Prohibitions**: For sentences intended to stop an action, the **Active Voice** uses **Do not** or **Don't**. The corresponding **Passive Voice** uses the structure **Let + Object + not + be + V3**.
 
• **Tense Consistency**: Imperative sentences do not typically use modal auxiliaries like **will** or **won't** in their standard form, as those indicate the **Future Indefinite Tense** rather than an immediate command or prohibition.
 
• **Subject-Verb Relationship**: In the active form, the implied subject **You** is the agent performing the action of 'repeating'. In the passive form, the focus shifts to the **Object** (the mistake) receiving the action.
 
 
</ul
